title: Three rules for the opening
line: Take the center, bring out the knights and bishops, castle.

steps.text: The four squares in the middle are the center. A piece there reaches the most squares.
Take the center with a pawn.

wrong.a2a3: That pawn does nothing for the center.

steps.hint: Move a pawn in front of the king or the queen.
steps.after: A pawn in the center, and lines open for the pieces behind it.

steps.text: Knights come out first. Tap both of them.

wrong.c1: That is a bishop. The knights stand next to the rooks.

steps.after: Each knight has a square toward the center.

steps.text: Bring a knight out toward the center.

wrong.g1h3: On the edge the knight reaches fewer squares.
wrong.b1a3: On the edge the knight reaches fewer squares.

steps.hint: Toward the center means f3 or c3.
steps.after: The knight reaches the center from there.

steps.text: Then the bishops come out, and the king castles to a safe corner.

summary: Take the center, bring out the knights and bishops, then castle.
